text:
anya: Quick thread (7m). We need a defensible, customer-facing promise for multi-region routing + tenant isolation to include in the 90-day roadmap doc. I want clean launch gates we can show sales/legal.

mason: From eng: three consumer-facing commitments make sense: 1) Region latency band, 2) Isolation tiering (opt-in contractual reserve vs shared), 3) Controlled failover behavior. Each must map to tests.

sarah: Product ask: one-sentence marketing promise + an appendix with concrete gates. Sales wants plain english, legal wants measurable acceptance tests.

rachel: Customer feedback: enterprise trials always ask "how do you prevent noisy neighbors" and "what happens in region failover?" They care about demoable runbooks.

tom: Ops perspective: if we offer contractual isolation we need reserved compute slices, eviction rules, and a documented billing uplift. Also automation labels so we can carve and reassign.

anya: Draft sellable pledge (very short): "Predictable latency across your chosen regions, and isolation tiers that guarantee reduced noisy-neighbor impact — backed by verifiable acceptance tests." Thoughts?

sarah: Nice. For launch gates, propose two parallel tracks: Hosted (self-serve) and Dedicated (contracted). Hosted: best-effort with documented fallbacks. Dedicated: contractual isolation subject to acceptance tests.

mason: Proposed acceptance tests (eng-readable):
- isolation_harness_v1: run 50k cross-tenant probes; zero KV namespace collisions observed
- routing_latency_check: synthetic workload across regions verifying P50/P95/P99 within declared band under 70% target load
- failover_drill: scripted region outage replay with end-to-end RTO measurement < 60s for reserved slices, <120s for best-effort
- canary_policy: 1% traffic for 24h -> increase rule with auto-rollback if error spike > 0.75%

rachel: Can we make the numbers customer-friendly? Sales prefers: "Gold: reserved, 60s RTO; Silver: best-effort, 120s RTO; Bronze: shared best-effort."

mason: Fine, but callouts: Gold requires warm reserved slices and onboarding runbook. We'll flag the cost delta.

legal-bot: FYI: any SLA wording with exact numbers will require a standard remedy clause. Recommend product provide a sample contract clause for review.

sarah: I'll draft the one-pager and sample clause once eng posts the exact acceptance test names and short descriptions. Include a "how to qualify" checklist.

anya: Ops automation ask: we need policy templates now (reserved-slice, shared-shared, preemptible-evict). DSL can follow, but templates + UI enablement must be in scope for the first launch.

tom: Agree. Templates should map to runtime knobs we can set: batching cap, KV cache policy, quantization profile, eviction thresholds. We'll publish the mapping table.

mason: Action items:
- eng (mason): finalize acceptance test definitions + quick-run commands for infra (ETA Mon)
- runtime (ben): publish runtime knob table mapping to tiers (ETA Tue)
- ops (tom): draft eviction + carveout templates and automation labels (ETA Tue)
- product (sarah + anya): draft sales one-pager + sample SLA language for legal (ETA Thu)
- legal: review sample clause and flag required remedy language (ETA Fri)
- release-bot: create tracking ticket when eng posts tests

release-bot: Created ticket PROD-4412: "Multi-region routing & isolation: customer pledge + launch gates" assigned to mason.

mason: I'll drop a stubbed `isolation_harness_v1` script in infra repo and add a README with how to run the 50k probe test.

anya: Great. We'll review the one-pager in Friday's roadmap review and call the gating checklist "Routing & Isolation: Launchable". Keep follow-ups short here. :spiral_calendar: 

sarah: noted. will ping once tests are posted.

rachel: Thanks team. Sales will run the pledge by two pilot customers this week and report back.

anya: End thread — thanks. :thumbsup:
